title: 3.6.16 Lab: Pass-by-Reference Capstone Practice
description: Build a small scorebook that adds scores without harming the caller's array, and a function that updates an object's property the caller can see. Auto-graded.

steps.title: A safe function that returns a new array
steps.instructions: Define addScore(scores, score) that returns a NEW array containing the old scores plus the new one, without changing the array it was given. Use spread to build the new array.

steps.title: A function that mutates a property on purpose
steps.instructions: Define recordPlay(song) that increases a plays property on the object it is given by 1. This one is meant to change the caller's object, because a play count is shared state.

steps.title: A deep-copy function for a nested structure
steps.instructions: Define copyBook(library) that returns a deep copy of an object holding a nested array, using structuredClone, so the caller's library is never touched when the copy changes.

steps.title: Demonstrate all three
steps.instructions: Call each function and log the caller's data before and after. Prove addScore and copyBook leave the originals alone, while recordPlay changes the object the caller sees.

requirements.hint: Add 1 to the song's plays property by assigning to it. This one is meant to change the caller's object.

requirements.hint: copyBook should return a deep copy. The work is done by structuredClone inside copyBook.

requirements.description: Code calls structuredClone for a deep copy Help: 3.6.9 (Side Effects and Copies)
requirements.hint: Pass the library to structuredClone so changes to the copy's nested array never reach the original.

requirements.title: results logged
requirements.description: Code calls console.log. Help: 3.6.10 (Defensive Copying: [...] and {...})
requirements.hint: Log the caller's data before and after each call to show which function changed it.

requirements.title: addScore returns a new array and leaves the original alone
requirements.description: addScore([10, 20], 30) returns [10, 20, 30] and the array passed in is still [10, 20]. Help: 3.6.10 (Defensive Copying)
requirements.hint: Return a new array built with spread: [...scores, score]. Do not push onto scores.

requirements.title: recordPlay raises plays on the object it is given
requirements.description: recordPlay({ title: "x", plays: 4 }) leaves that same object with plays 5. Help: 3.6.5 (Changing vs. Reassigning)
requirements.hint: recordPlay must change the plays property of the song it receives. Do not copy here: a play count is shared state.

requirements.title: copyBook returns a deep copy
requirements.description: Changing the nested array of copyBook(library) leaves library.books unchanged. Help: 3.6.9 (Side Effects and Copies)
requirements.hint: Return structuredClone(library). A spread copy or returning the same object would still share the nested array.

checks.expr: typeof copyBook === 'function' && (l => { const c = copyBook(l); c.books.push('C'); return c !== l && c.books !== l.books && l.books.length === 2 && c.books.length === 3; })({ name: 'S', books: ['A', 'B'] })
checks.fail: copyBook should give back a deep copy: after pushing onto the copy's books, the original library.books must still have its two items.

checks.expr: typeof copyBook === 'function' && (() => { const o = globalThis.structuredClone; let last; globalThis.structuredClone = (...a) => (last = o(...a)); let r; try { r = copyBook({ name: 'S', books: ['A', 'B'] }); } finally { globalThis.structuredClone = o; } return last !== undefined && (r === last || (!!r && !!last && r.books === last.books)); })()
checks.fail: copyBook should make its copy by calling structuredClone on the library and returning that result (a call whose result is thrown away, or a copy made some other way, does not count).

requirements.title: the callers' data is printed

requirements.hint: Print the scores array, the song object and the library before and after each call, so the output shows what each function did.

checks.fail: Print the caller's data (the scores, the song's plays and the library's books) before and after each call, at least three lines, so the output shows which function changed what.
